==English== {{wp|}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ew-|id1=perceive}} From {{inh|en|enm|audience}}, from {{der|en|frm|audience}}, from {{der|en|fro|audience}}, from {{der|en|la|audientia}}, from present participle {{m|la|audiēns||hearing}}, from verb {{m|la|audiō||to hear}}. {{doublet|en|audiencia}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈɔːdi.əns/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈoːdɪjəns/|a=SSB}} ** {{audio|en|Audience_(standard_British_pronunciation).ogg |a=SSB}} * {{a|en|US}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɔ.di.əns/|[ˈɔ.ɾi.əns]|a=non-cot-caught}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɑ.di.əns/|[ˈɑ.ɾi.əns]|a=cot-caught}} *** {{audio|en|en-us-audience.ogg|a=US,cot-caught}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈɒ.di.əns/|[ˈɒ.ɾi.əns]|a=CA}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈoːdi.əns/|[ˈoːɾi.əns]|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈɔ.de.əns/|a=Scotland}} * {{hyphenation|en|au|di| ence}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # A [[group]] of people within hearing; specifically, a large gathering of people listening to or watching a [[performance]], [[speech]], etc. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} #: {{ux|en|We joined the '''audience''' just as the lights went down.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=V|page=26|passage=One saint's day in mid-term a certain newly appointed suffragan-bishop came to the school chapel, and there preached on “The Inner Life.”  He at once secured attention by his informal method, and when presently the coughing of Jarvis {{...}} interrupted the sermon, he altogether captivated his '''audience''' with a remark about cough lozenges being cheap and easily procurable.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1952|month=February|author=H. C. Casserley|title=Permanent Wayfarings|journal=Railway Magazine|page=77|text=My '''audience''' to this not-too-easy operation was a small group of Scottish school lasses, who seemed (perhaps naturally) to find the proceedings somewhat mysterious, but at any rate amusing. I wished they would go away, but they didn't, so I had to get on with the job to the accompaniment of a background of giggles!}} # {{lb|en|now|_|rare}} [[hearing|Hearing]]; the condition or state of hearing or listening. {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Luke|7|1|lxxxiiij|verso=1|text=WHen he had ended all his ſayingꝭ in the '''audience''' of the people / he entred ĩto Capernaum.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1861|title=Eclectic Magazine, and Monthly Edition of the Living Age|page=453 |text=... groans and roarings full of plaintive anger, the force of which can only be realized by actual '''audience'''. When solicited by the jerking of their noses, they condescend to kneel down and tuck their legs under them;{{nb...}}}} # A [[widespread]] or [[nationwide]] viewing or listening [[public]], as of a [[television|TV]] or [[radio]] [[network]] or [[program]]. # {{senseid|en|meeting}} A [[formal]] meeting with a [[state]] or [[religious]] [[dignitary]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}} #: {{ux|en|She managed to get an '''audience''' with the Pope.}} #* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|system=PC|scene=Citadel|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|text=Captain Anderson: Sounds like you convinced the Council to give us an '''audience'''.
Ambassador Udina: They were not happy about it. Saren's their top agent. They don't like him being accused of treason.}} # The [[readership]] of a [[book]] or other [[written]] [[publication]]. {{defdate|from 19th c.}} #: {{ux|en|"Private Eye" has a small but faithful '''audience'''.}} # A [[following]]. {{defdate|from 20th c.}} #: {{ux|en|The opera singer expanded his '''audience''' by singing songs from the shows.}} # {{lb|en|historical}} An [[audiencia]] (judicial court of the Spanish empire), or the [[territory]] administered by it. ====Usage notes==== * In some lects, ''audience'' is used as a [[plurale tantum]]. *: ''The audience are getting restless.'' ====Synonyms==== * {{l|en|hearership}}, {{l|en|listenership}} * {{sense|large gathering of people watching a performance}} {{l|en|spectators}}, {{l|en|crowd}} ====Derived terms====
